title: Search Autocomplete
oneLine: Serve top-K suggestions from a compact prefix index, rebuild from aggregated search logs, and overlay fresh trends with strict latency and safety controls.
opening: The read path must be extremely fast, so I would precompute the top K suggestions for each relevant prefix in a trie or prefix-key store and serve it from memory/cache. The write/data path is separate: search/query events enter a log, are normalized and aggregated by frequency, recency, locale, and quality, then a builder creates a new immutable prefix index. The index is rolled out atomically by version. To capture breaking trends between batch builds, a small real-time delta store is merged with the baseline at query time under a tight deadline. Suggestions are filtered for policy, spelling, locale, and personalization, and popularity uses time decay so old queries do not dominate forever.
ask: Prefix only, typo tolerance, or semantic suggestions?
Global, locale-specific, personalized, or all three?
What is the p99 latency and freshness target?
How are harmful, private, or low-quality queries filtered?
scale: Keystroke QPS can be several times search QPS because each query produces multiple prefixes.
Precompute only meaningful prefixes—often from length 2 or 3—and cache top K at nodes.
Index versions are immutable so rollout and rollback are atomic.

decisions.default: Trie/prefix FST or prefix-key store with cached top K.
decisions.why: Lookup is proportional to prefix length and avoids scanning all candidates.
decisions.switch: Search engine completion suggester for fuzzy matching, multilingual analysis, and operational convenience.

decisions.default: Immutable batch baseline plus bounded real-time overlay.
decisions.why: Batch gives quality and compactness; overlay gives freshness without rebuilding constantly.
decisions.switch: Pure batch for stable enterprise terms; streaming-heavy for news/trends.

decisions.default: Shard by normalized prefix range or first characters, with replicas for hot ranges.
decisions.switch: Replicate the whole compact index when it fits in memory; this simplifies latency and availability.

decisions.default: Merge a small user/segment candidate list after global retrieval.
decisions.why: A fully personalized trie per user is too costly.
decisions.switch: Disable or privacy-gate personalization for sensitive contexts.

deepDives.title: Ranking
points: Combine frequency, recency decay, click/success quality, locale, and policy score.
Use stable tie-breaking to avoid flicker between keystrokes.
Penalize spam/manipulation and repeated bot traffic.

deepDives.title: Index rollout
points: Build offline, validate coverage/size/safety, publish a version manifest, then switch readers atomically.
Keep previous version warm for rollback.
Warm caches before full traffic cutover.

deepDives.title: Privacy
points: Apply k-anonymity/minimum-count thresholds before a query becomes public.
Remove PII and sensitive terms from training logs.

failures.response: Serve immutable baseline; autocomplete should remain available with reduced freshness.
Versioned atomic rollout, safety validation, canary traffic, and instant rollback.
Replicate/cache top prefixes at edge and coalesce identical requests.
PII filtering, minimum support thresholds, delayed publication, and audit/red-team testing.

questions.q: Why cache top K at every trie node?
questions.a: Then a lookup walks the prefix and returns immediately rather than traversing the entire subtree and sorting at request time. The trade-off is extra build-time memory.
Use fuzzy candidate generation—edit-distance automata, n-grams, or a search engine suggester—then rank under a strict candidate/latency budget.

questions.q: How do you update without downtime?
questions.a: Build an immutable version, distribute and warm it, switch a small manifest/pointer atomically, and retain the old version for rollback.
Aggregate authenticated/quality-weighted events, rate-limit sources, detect bot bursts, use time decay and trust features, and require minimum independent users.

mistakes: Scanning a database with LIKE prefix at internet scale
Rebuilding the only live trie in place
Publishing rare queries without privacy thresholds
seniorSignal: Separate candidate generation, ranking, freshness overlay, safety, and immutable rollout. Treat autocomplete as a high-QPS serving system plus an offline data product.
implementation: Compact trie/FST loaded in-process or Redis for smaller scale
Edge cache for hot prefixes and circuit-broken personalization
